title: glosa claim-evidence-theory matrix row
description: tier: Dr (specified; independently unreviewed). One row per (claim x source use) of the Claim-Evidence-Theory matrix narrated by methodology/P26_claim_evidence_theory_matrix.md (founder instruction 2026-09-25). A row is a JOIN, never a second home: the claim's canonical text lives on claim_card (claim_id -> claim_card.claim_id, statement.text), the passage/verification lives on citation_card (source -> citation_card.id, exact_passage, claim_match_verified, audit), and the search that produced the source lives on search_log. What this row adds, and is the only home of: the construct the source is used for, the source's genre, its role in the three-tier citation rule, what the passage supports, what it does NOT support, rival evidence, and where in the manuscript it is used. Namespace https://glosa.example/ is a placeholder.

claim_id.description: Pointer to claim_card.claim_id (schema/claim_card.schema.json). The claim's canonical wording lives there, not here.

claim_label.description: Short display handle so a human can read the matrix without a join. NOT the claim's canonical text (that is claim_card.statement.text); when the two disagree, the claim card wins and this label is stale.

construct.description: The construct (named concept) this source is being used for. The three-tier citation rule (P26 item g) is evaluated per distinct construct value across the matrix.

source.description: Pointer to citation_card.id (schema/citation_card.schema.json). One citation card = one citation USE, so the row grain (claim x source) and the card grain coincide.

source_type.description: Genre of the cited source itself (what kind of object it is), independent of its role for this construct.

construct_tier_role.description: Role in the three-tier citation rule per construct (P26 item g): originating_source (where the construct was first stated, read directly -- never through a review), current_synthesis (a recent integrating account), critical_or_contradictory (evidence or argument against, or a documented limit), supporting_only (backs a premise without filling one of the three tiers).

supports.description: What the cited passage supports, stated no wider than citation_card.exact_passage allows.

does_not_support.description: What the passage does NOT support, even though a reader might assume it does. Required and non-empty: stating the boundary is the point of the row (NC-18 source existence != claim support; NC-57 claim scope <= evidence scope).

rival_evidence.description: Pointers to citation cards (cite-...) or other matrix rows (cem-...) carrying evidence that cuts against this row's use. May be empty only with rival_search_ref naming the search whose challenge query family returned nothing (NC-27: not found != does not exist).

rival_search_ref.description: search_log.id whose queries.challenge family was run for this claim/construct.

used_in_section.description: Manuscript section anchors where this source is cited for this claim. Empty = carded but not used in the draft (legal; a row with no use is still a record of what was read).

mechanism_ref.description: Optional pointer to the theory_evidence_falsifier_row (tef-...) whose logical_basis states the mechanism this row's citation supports a part of (P26 item h: mechanism first, cite parts).

tier.description: Tier of this row as a readout (normally Dr until the linked citation_card.audit.status is VERIFIED by a checker who is not the maker).

allOf.description: Empty rival_evidence requires a named challenge search (P05, NC-27).
